Subject: Demo Spotlight: one-pager final + runbook / QA slots

Team — quick kickoff for the SaaS Summit spotlight we have on Sept 14. Attached is the current one-pager (demo-onepager-v2.pdf) and a minimal brief. Two asks: 

1) Can someone take the lead on tightening the one-pager to a single, scannable side? Focus: value props (latency/cost/reliability), 3 bullet customer impact lines, one short customer quote.

2) We need a solid runbook and 20–30m dry-run window this week to validate AV + the shortened demo flow. Prefer morning slots (PST) if possible.

Notes: sponsor wants a 30s highlight clip (we’ll capture a short segment during the final run). Karthik — confirm greenroom / slide handoff requirements and whether sponsor wants co-branding on the one-pager.

Attachments: demo-onepager-v2.pdf (attached).

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Field Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo Spotlight: one-pager final + runbook / QA slots

Sounds good — I can own the one-pager edit. Quick thoughts after a skim:
- Lead with a 1-line problem statement ("Make inference predictable and economical at scale") then 3 bullets: predictable latency, reserved capacity, and cost controls (batching/caching).
- Move the customer metric up (e.g., "Reduced per-token cost 3x for X workload"). Need a verified stat from the CS team — Marissa, can you confirm?
- Suggest swapping the technical appendix to a tiny 2-line "How it works" section and move implementation notes to the runbook.

I attached a light runbook checklist (runbook-demo-checklist.xlsx) with proposed checkpoints (stage mic check, streaming test, model fallback validation, recording capture).

For dry runs: I’m available 08/24 09:00–10:30 or 08/25 08:30–10:00 PST. Ava, can you confirm which model variant you want to rehearse (gpt-like-13b-quant vs. 7b-opt)?

—Sean
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo Spotlight: one-pager final + runbook / QA slots

Adding the demo-engineer perspective — thanks Sean.

Recommended rehearsal configuration:
- Model: 13B-quant variant (g13b-q) for live demo to show latency under load; fallback to 7b-opt for backup.
- Sequence length: prepare 1.2k–1.5k typical prompt (we should exercise KV cache behavior).
- Prefix caching: enable for the intro prompt to avoid warm-start latency.
- Env: stage cluster in us-west-2, single-instance warm-up, no autoscale during capture.

Demo script notes attached (demo-script-v1.3.txt) — highlights: 1) 60s customer problem, 2) 90s live prompt to show latency/cost, 3) 30s sponsor highlight capture. Keep transitions tight; plan to use two laptops (presenter + capture).

I’ll join the 08/24 09:00 PST slot if you want an earlier run, otherwise 08/25 09:00 PST works for final capture.

—Ava
Product Demo Engineer
